description.narrative: Oxfam is a global movement for change that empowers people to create a secure future, just and free from poverty. We believe that everyone has a right to safety, security, a livelihood, and a say in decisions that affect them. We seek a world in which everyone can speak up to power, demand and claim their human rights, and build a better future for themselves. We recognize that we cannot achieve this on our own but as a collective power. We, therefore, work in partnership with local and grass-root organizations, civil society, individuals, volunteers, the private sector, and the Government. Oxfam started working in Uganda in the 1960s. Since then, we have implemented both development and humanitarian programs to support practical and innovative ways for people to lift themselves out of poverty. Oxfam envisions Uganda free of extreme inequality and injustice; a society where citizens and particularly women across all age groups claim and exercise their rights and responsibilities and can influence decisions that affect their lives. Our one country program is hinged on three thematic goals that aim to promote women’s rights, good governance and accountability, resilient livelihoods, as well as humanitarian preparedness and response. Oxfam also believes that besides saving lives, it is imperative to strengthen humanitarian capacity at a local level. This ensures better, quicker and cost-effective preparedness and response to humanitarian situations. Hence, the organization invests in actions that strengthen the capacity of local humanitarian actors in all our areas of work. Our Vision is Uganda free of inequality and Injustice. A society where people, particularly women and young people, claim and exercise their rights and responsibilities and influence decisions that affect their lives. Our work is guided by the Country Strategic Framework (CSF) (2021-2030) which is organized around four themes: Governance and Accountability, Resilient Livelihoods, Humanitarian preparedness and response and Gender Justice and Women Rights. All the themes work towards influencing policy and practice, youth and women empowerment, inclusive participation in decision making at various levels, and capacity. Description of the crisis (including number of affected, timeline, number of affected Oxfam has reached to date etc): According to the Uganda National Meteorological Authority (UNMA), weather outlook (MAM) 2026, most disaster-prone regions in the country will continue to receive heavy rainfall with the highest peak of rainfall which will be above the normal trend thus this will still create high chances of increased flooding and landslide events in many parts of the country. Currently most of the areas in the High-altitude zones are soggy with water oozing from the ground at different points. This is an indicator of the increased risk of landslides in these areas, and allthe lowlands are flooded. The implication of the current forecast The forecast of near normal to above normal during the MAM 2026 season is likely to have significant implications on social economic activities including agriculture and food security health, energy and water resources among others. Areas projected to receive near normal rainfall are expected to receive rainfall amounts within their long-term climatological averages. This implies that rainfall is most likely to be sufficient to support normal agricultural production and other social economic activities that are dependent on seasonal rainfall. It’s also worth noting that, localised episodic flash floods events may occur in areas that are expected to receive near normal rainfall because of isolated heavy down pours. Similarly in localised areas are expected to receive above normal rainfall, poor rainfall distribution may as well occur. In alignment with WFP’s ‘Saving Lives and Changing Lives’ mandate, WFP remains a critical partner to the Government of Uganda in the response to emergencies through the provision of both food assistance and supply chain (logistical support) services as below: - In 2020 and 2021, WFP provided General Food Assistance to refugees living in Kampala whose livelihoods had been disrupted by COVID-19 restrictions. - 2022 EVD outbreak, WFP provided General Food Assistance to households directly affected in Mubende, Kassanda and Jinja districts. - 2023 WFP supported emergency food assistance to households displaced by floods and landslides in Kisoro - In 2024 WFP assistance floods victims in Ntoroko and Kasese districts - In 2025 WFP is supporting government respond to the ongoing Mpox disease outbreak, currently providing meals to Mpox patients admitted in treatment centres across the country. Oxfam in Uganda responded to a World Food Programme (WFP) call for Expressions of Interest for emergency response. Our application was successful and assessed as the best fit for disaster response in the country. As a result, WFP proactively identified and selected Oxfam in Uganda and has signed a 24-month framework agreement to support our emergency response implementation. Under this agreement, Oxfam is expected to deliver rapid responses within 72 hours of disaster onset. Given this partnership and the operational expectations, it entails, Oxfam in Uganda must be fully prepared to meet rapid response requirements and deliver effective, accountable humanitarian assistance. To ensure readiness and consistent quality of response, we require targeted investments in personnel training and operational systems. Project description / activities (including numbers to be reached): Oxfam’s Humanitarian Emergency Team (HET) plays a central role in rapid humanitarian mobilization, assessment, response design, and coordination. With increasing frequency of shocks, conflict, climate‑induced disasters, epidemics, and economic crises, there is growing reliance on Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) as an efficient, scalable, and dignity‑enhancing response modality. To ensure high‑quality, timely, accountable, and safe CVA and multisector emergency operations, HET members require updated skills in: CVA design and delivery, Cash feasibility and market assessments, Risk analysis and mitigation, Protection, gender, and safeguarding integration, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for CVA and emergency response, Oxfam Emergency Response Protocol (ERP) and humanitarian principles, Coordination, reporting, and compliance, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and Humanitarian Response plan. This 5‑day training is designed to strengthen HET capacity to lead, support, and monitor high‑quality humanitarian responses in alignment with Oxfam standards and global best practices. Main objectives. • Understand and apply Oxfam’s Emergency Response Protocol (ERP), humanitarian principles, and minimum preparedness requirements. • Design and implement CVA interventions using market assessments, response option analysis, transfer value calculation, delivery mechanisms,and risk mitigation approaches. • Use and operationalize CVA Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), including targeting, registration, verification, delivery, reconciliation, and documentation. • Integrate protection, gender, safeguarding, MEAL, and AAP standards into CVA and emergency operations. • Strengthen coordination with clusters, local authorities, financial service providers, and partners for harmonized cash-based programming. • Apply tools for rapid assessments, market assessments, cash feasibility analysis, and risk assessments during emergencies. • Improve reporting, compliance, and documentation in line with Oxfam and donor requirements Estimated use

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib is one of the 17 national affiliates of the Oxfam International Confederation. It started life in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Working together in confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education forall, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam established this country office to support local organizations and projects. Through this local office Oxfam Novib directly contributes towards this project’s implementation.
